grid.layout: int16 elevation m (-32768 = no data), then uint8 slope deg (255 = no data), then uint8 roughness in 0.1 m (255 = no data); rows run north to south

stops.name: Stop 1
stops.title: Polygon Heaven: Fractured Bedrock
stops.blurb: Curiosity investigated polygon-shaped cracks in the bedrock that may have formed as ancient sediments dried out or through later groundwater activity, offering clues about Mars' changing environment.

stops.name: Stop 2
stops.title: Early Boxwork Bedrock
stops.blurb: Curiosity examined rocky terrain near the emerging boxwork formations, investigating bedrock textures and chemistry to better understand the region's geological history.

stops.name: Stop 3
stops.title: First Boxwork Ridge
stops.blurb: One of Curiosity's first close investigations of boxwork formations, where mineral deposits from ancient groundwater may reveal Mars' past water history.

stops.name: Stop 4
stops.title: Boxwork Bedrock & Troughs
stops.blurb: Curiosity studied exposed bedrock and troughs near emerging boxwork ridges, providing evidence to investigate how Martian rocks were altered and eroded.

stops.name: Stop 5
stops.title: Altadena Drill Site
stops.blurb: Curiosity drilled into ancient boxwork-region bedrock here and analyzed the rock powder for minerals and chemical clues about Mars' past water conditions.

stops.name: Stop 6
stops.title: Copacabana-Copiapo Boxwork Trough
stops.blurb: Curiosity studied fractured bedrock inside a boxwork trough to investigate mineral deposits and chemical evidence of ancient groundwater activity.

stops.name: Stop 7
stops.title: Hornitos Veined Bedrock
stops.blurb: Curiosity examined possible mineral veins cutting through the bedrock, offering clues about ancient groundwater activity in Gale Crater.

stops.name: Stop 8
stops.title: Guapay Ridges & Troughs
stops.blurb: Curiosity compared harder, resistant bedrock with lower, eroded troughs to understand why different parts of the boxwork terrain weather differently.
